source.title: Extracting Paragraphs from LLM Token Activations
source.authors: Nicholas Pochinkov; A. Benoit; Lovkush Agarwal; Zainab Ali Majid; Lucile Ter-Minassian

page_placements.theme: Local, recent-context basis of next-token and planning decisions

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a transition-token activation carries information about later paragraph content using activation transplantation and semantic-similarity measures, rather than the original token-level prediction methods.
record.gate_note: Section 2 measures paragraph-related attention patterns and activation similarity during generated text, but does not measure whether an earlier state represents a later token or causally changes intervening text; no row recorded for those results. Section 3 compares text generated after transferring activations with neutral-prompt generations, including controls given one or two initial words. The paper cites results from other studies in its related-work discussion; those are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: In Gemma 2 9b, all-layer activations at one '\n\n' token were transplanted into a neutral prompt. Text generated afterwards was compared by sentence-embedding distance with controls given 0, 1 or 2 'cheat' first words. This measures, by a different method, how much one position's state carries about tokens further ahead (V2), and how shallow that look-ahead is (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: a single '\n\n' token's activations encode substantial information about the next paragraph, and transplanting them yields semantically similar text. Most, but not all, of this information seems contained in the first two generated tokens.
record.recipe_differences: Uses all-layer activation transplantation at a paragraph transition and sentence-embedding cosine distances, rather than token-level future-token prediction or rhyme-word interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The comparison depends on neutral prompts with zero, one, or two initial cheat tokens; transferred generations remain closer than neutral2. The paper also reports weaker and anecdotal topic capture for complex-topic examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 2: attention weights stay almost entirely within the current paragraph. Attention-output cosine similarity rises within paragraphs and falls across them through about layer 18, and the distinction fades from layer 30 onward.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM activations encode paragraph/topic structure during generation, distinct from look-ahead.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says the code is available anonymously but gives no URL in the text
record.problems: Only one model is tested. The main measure is sentence-embedding cosine distance, not exact future-token prediction. The transfer copies activations from all layers, including the final layer, and does not isolate the causal contribution of specific features. The paper notes abrupt topic switches may not represent realistic text. Complex-topic tests are explicitly anecdotal and not full experiments. A few generations that did not follow the intended structure were excluded from the attention analysis.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results left out. Section 2 attention-weight and attention-output similarity analyses were not recorded as rows because they do not measure whether the transition-token state represents future tokens or whether changing it affects later generated text.

untested.parts: No rhyming verse or frontier-model rhyme intervention.

Does not test whether features at '\n\n' are computed because they help later positions rather than as a byproduct of next-token prediction. The all-layer transplant only shows the information is present and usable.
No rhyme planning in open models.
No reasoning, chess, Sokoban or other non-text task; prose paragraphs only.
No exact future-token prediction at specific offsets; semantic similarity only. One model only.

record.verdict_notes: Preprint, single model (Gemma 2 9b). The transplant covers all layers, including the final layer; neutral1 and neutral2 address the resulting next-token advantage. Abrupt topic switches are artificial. Complex-topic evidence is anecdotal. The record's V3 labels were dropped: nothing here separates pre-caching from byproduct features.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse task, candidate rhyme words, or intervention on rhyme choices.
Measures semantic similarity of generated paragraphs, not exact prediction of particular tokens several positions ahead.
Does not isolate particular features or establish why they were computed; it tests transfer of the transition-token activations, not the model's computation process in natural generation.
No rhyme-planning experiment in open-weight models or use of open attribution-graph or probing tools.
No multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or other task or architecture is tested.
The paper does not identify specific local next-token features or heuristics, and its more complex-topic tests are anecdotal rather than full experiments.

rows.subject: Gemma 2, 9b
rows.operation_detail: Generated from the neutral prompt without activation transplantation (neutral0); compared by cosine distance to the original generation.
rows.measure: Mean cosine distance to original generation, with standard deviation
rows.baseline: Original generation is the reference for cosine distance; no numerical chance level stated
rows.note: Aggregate over 1,000 original contexts. Control generation without transferred activations; the paper reports low similarity relative to transferred generations.
rows.check: Control (neutral0, no transplant), not a model effect. 0.973 is the baseline for r4. It shows no information about the original paragraph, as expected. Removed V3: the measure cannot show why features were computed.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V2 and V6. Neutral0 is a control without access to the original context or transferred activations.
source_check.problem: An uninformed control cannot establish absence of future-token information or planning in the original model state.

rows.subject: Gemma 2, 9b
rows.operation_detail: Generated from the neutral prompt with one initial word from the original paragraph as a cheat token; compared by cosine distance to the original generation.
rows.measure: Mean cosine distance to original generation, with standard deviation
rows.baseline: Original generation is the reference for cosine distance; no numerical chance level stated
rows.note: Aggregate over 1,000 original contexts. This control is closer to the original generation than neutral0, but the paper reports transferred generations are closer.
rows.check: Control (neutral1). Its closeness comes from a supplied cheat word, not from planning in the model. Its 'partial' state is meaningless on its own; it serves only as a baseline for r4. Removed V3.

rows.subject: Gemma 2, 9b
rows.operation_detail: Generated from the neutral prompt with two initial words from the original paragraph as cheat tokens; compared by cosine distance to the original generation.
rows.measure: Mean cosine distance to original generation, with standard deviation
rows.baseline: Original generation is the reference for cosine distance; transferred generations are the reported comparison
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation 0.239; comparison with transferred: t-statistic -8.79, p = 3.19 × 10−18
rows.note: Aggregate over 1,000 original contexts. This baseline is much closer than neutral0 and neutral1; the transferred condition is still closer.
rows.check: Control (neutral2, two cheat words), 0.303. It is the key baseline for r4, not an effect in itself. Removed V3.

rows.subject: Gemma 2, 9b
rows.operation_detail: Transferred the double-newline token activations from the original context to the corresponding token in a neutral-prompt run across all model layers, including attention and MLP layers.
rows.measure: Mean cosine distance between generated text and the original generation, using sentence-transformer embeddings
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation 0.210; versus neutral2, t-statistic -8.79, p = 3.19 × 10−18
rows.note: Aggregate over 1,000 original contexts. The authors report transferred generations are closer to the original than neutral0, neutral1, and neutral2. The transfer includes final-layer activations, which the authors note may provide a next-token advantage; neutral1 and neutral2 were added as controls.
rows.check: State is relative to the look-ahead effect (V2). Transferred 0.214 vs neutral2 0.303, t=-8.79, p=3.19e-18: information beyond the first two words. For V6 this cuts against a strictly two-token horizon, but the gap is modest. The authors say most information sits in the first two tokens. Removed V3: an all-layer transplant does not show features were computed for later positions rather than as a byproduct.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for the linked V2 and V6 claims. All-layer transplantation improves paragraph-level semantic similarity: 0.214 (SD 0.210) versus 0.303 (SD 0.239), t=-8.79, p=3.19×10^-18.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3; Appendix A, Table 1 and preceding significance-test paragraph.
source_check.problem: Paragraph-topic recovery using all layers does not establish single-hidden-state future-token prediction or determine the planning horizon.

relationships.condition: Gemma 2 9b, 1,000 contexts, transferred vs two-cheat-token control
relationships.reason: The transplant beats neutral2, so the content is not wholly explained by the first two words. The margin is modest (0.214 vs 0.303), and the authors say most information is in the first two tokens (r3, r4).
relationships.display_finding: Across 1,000 contexts, transplantation modestly outperformed the two-word control, with scores of 0.214 versus 0.303, although most information lay in the first two tokens.

relation.reason: The study experimentally tests future-paragraph information with transplantation and neutral controls; its results bear on look-ahead beyond verse.

tranche.reason: All-layer activation transplantation and paragraph-embedding comparisons provide a different method aimed at future-context information. This classification does not establish the narrower V2 or V6 claims.

source_check.notes: Paragraph-topic information from all layers at one position is relevant to V5, which has no listed verdict. The text declares anonymous code availability, contrary to the pack's code=n metadata.

statements.correction: Gemma 2 9b; 1,000 contexts; all-layer transition-token transplantation; mean paragraph-embedding cosine distances: transferred 0.214, neutral0 0.973, neutral1 0.616, neutral2 0.303; transferred versus neutral2 p=3.19×10^-18; no single-layer or token-position prediction evaluation.
statements.problem: The study-specific numbers and semantic-recovery description are correct, but the experiment uses all layers at one position and does not establish V2's single-hidden-state future-token claim.

statements.correction: Appendix A: complex-topic trials are anecdotal; no full experiment; alternative energy storage becomes energy sources; astrophysics becomes AI; renewable-energy phrase appears in two of three displayed completions.
statements.problem: The anecdotal descriptions are accurate; they establish imperfect topic recovery, rather than a measured fine-detail deficit or a limitation of V2's specified token-prediction effect.

statements.correction: Complex-topic transplantation sometimes loses the intended topic; no full complex-topic experiment; no planning-horizon measurement or comparison of pre-boundary and boundary states.
statements.problem: The astrophysics-to-AI example and anecdotal qualification are correct, but this study does not compare positions before the boundary or measure how many tokens ahead planning extends.

statements.correction: Transferred mean cosine distance 0.214 (SD 0.210); neutral2 0.303 (SD 0.239); authors conclude most, but not all, contextual information appears contained in the first two generated tokens; no quantified planning horizon.
statements.problem: The measurements and authors' conclusion are accurate, but outperforming a two-cheat-token baseline does not contradict a horizon of a few tokens or establish independence from local cues.
